title: Workload reservoirs: GPU lease allocator and predictive noisy-workload attenuation
creator: Anika Ramesh
description:
Problem: In Dedicated pools we still see intermittent customer-visible throughput collapses when a small set of aggressive workloads (short, high-concurrency generation) overwhelm shared resources and push other customers past throughput/latency SLOs. Existing approaches (hard slices, strict preemption) are too rigid for common mixed workloads and lead to capacity underutilization or noisy churn during bursts.

Goal: Implement a GPU lease allocator that hands out short-duration 'reservoir' leases to active workloads, enforce a per-customer minimum throughput contract, and introduce a predictive attenuation layer that proactively reduces weight of fingerprinted noisy generators before hard evictions. The feature should: (1) preserve guaranteed throughput floors for committed customers, (2) reduce 95th-tail latency amplification due to noisy neighbors by >70% in our pilot, (3) integrate with autoscaling to provision ephemeral lanes before SLA breaches, and (4) provide observability and manual remediation hooks in the Console.

High-level design:
- Lease allocator: on request admission we allocate a reservoir token bundle for a short epoch (default 15s) describing allowed burst credits and concurrency baseline. Leases are cheap to renew and trackable per-customer and per-route.
- Reservoir model: each GPU pool maintains a capacity reservoir. Active leases draw credits; reservoirs refill at controlled rates. If a customer's consumption nears their guaranteed floor, we prefer replenishing that customer's reservoir over granting new speculative leases.
- Predictive attenuation: fingerprint active requests by feature signals (sequence-length distribution, request inter-arrival, model-id, repeated prompt patterns). A trained classifier scores 'noisy-likelihood'. Instead of immediate preemption we apply an attenuation multiplier (0.5-0.9) to that workload's scheduling weight and reduce KV cache residency priority for speculative requests.
- Autoscale integration: when aggregate reservoir headroom drops below threshold (20%) and predicted SLO risk > 0.6, trigger an aggressive autoscale path that requests ephemeral lanes or spills to cheaper capacity with compatibility fallback.
- Enforcement: soft enforcement via token accounting and attenuation for first two degradations; hard enforcement (temporary lease denial / shaped queueing) only after repeated behavior or if guaranteed floors are at risk.

Trade-offs considered:
- Soft attenuation preserves customer experience for benign bursty traffic but can be gamed; we mitigate via rate-limited attenuation windows and audit logs.
- Aggressive autoscale reduces degradation but increases cost; we make this configurable per-customer and expose cost-vs-slo guidance in Console.
- Fingerprinting risks false positives; we will keep classifier conservative and require manual review mode in pilot accounts.

Deliverables: design doc, prototype runtime hooks (allocator + scorer), autoscale policy wiring, Console telemetry and remediation UI, rollout plan (pilot -> canary -> general availability).
comments: 2026-02-10 - Initial writeup: scoped feature to lease allocator + attenuation. Posted design doc to Confluence, requested architecture review.
2026-02-18 - Architecture review notes (Michael Chen): add KV-cache eviction priority tie-in and ensure lease metadata survives process restarts (persist to etcd). Scoped epoch length tunables.

2026-02-25 - Prototype implemented: allocator service + in-memory reservoirs on a single pool. Experiment script injected synthetic noisy clients. Results: baseline noisy neighbor caused 95th latency increase of 32%; prototype attenuation reduced that to 8% in controlled lab runs (see attached dashboard).

2026-03-03 - Integrations: wired attenuation multiplier into scheduler weight. Observed a small scheduling jitter at 5-10s after attenuation due to token refresh timing; plan to shift to epoch-aligned refresh to avoid micro-churn.
2026-03-09 - PM feedback (Riya Patel): expose per-customer 'cost-to-protect' estimate and allow customers to opt into aggressive autoscale in Console. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-12 - Blocker: missing high-cardinality telemetry for fingerprint features (sequence-length histograms per customer). Infra has a task to add lightweight aggregations (ENG-903219 referenced). Once available we can tune classifier thresholds in production-like environments.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot rollout to two dedicated pools with non-critical customers and no regression to existing SLOs (latency and throughput).
95th-tail noisy-neighbor amplification reduced to <10% in pilot pools compared to baseline. Live dashboards show reservoir headroom and lease churn.
Autoscale triggers respond within 60s of reservoir headroom breach and do not oscillate (cooldown enforced).
Console exposes per-customer 'protection budget' and manual soft-quarantine action; audit logs persisted for 90 days.
Operational runbook for investigating attenuation actions and reverting policy is published and validated in two tabletop drills.
